005package org.wpilib.command3;
006
007import java.util.List;
008import java.util.function.Consumer;
009import org.wpilib.annotation.NoDiscard;
010import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
011
012/**
013 * Generic interface to represent mechanisms on a robot. Commands can require sole ownership of a
014 * mechanism; when a command that requires a mechanism is running, no other commands may use it at
015 * the same time.
016 *
017 * <p>Even though this interface is named "Mechanism", it may be used to represent other physical
018 * hardware on a robot that should be controlled with commands - for example, an LED strip or a
019 * vision processor that can switch between different pipelines could be represented as mechanisms.
020 */
021public interface Mechanism {
022  /**
023   * Returns the scheduler under which this subsystem and its default commands are registered. The
024   * scheduler is also used to fetch running commands for the subsystem.
025   *
026   * @return The registered scheduler.
027   */
028  default Scheduler getRegisteredScheduler() {
029    return Scheduler.getDefault();
030  }
031
032  /**
033   * Marks this mechanism as being controllable when the robot is in a disabled mode. If a mechanism
034   * is not controllable, commands that require it cannot be scheduled when the robot is disabled
035   * and will be canceled when the robot enters a disabled mode.
036   *
037   * <p>By default, mechanisms are not controllable during disabled. Override this method to return
038   * {@code true} if the mechanism should be controllable during disabled modes.
039   *
040   * @return Whether this mechanism is controllable during disabled modes.
041   */
042  default boolean controllableDuringDisabled() {
043    return false;
044  }
045
046  /**
047   * Gets the name of this mechanism. This will default to the name of this mechanism's class.
048   *
049   * @return The name of the mechanism.
050   */
051  @NoDiscard
052  default String getName() {
053    return getClass().getSimpleName();
054  }
055
056  /**
057   * Sets the default command to run on the mechanism when no other command is scheduled. The
058   * default command's priority is effectively the minimum allowable priority for any command
059   * requiring a mechanism. For this reason, it's recommended that a default command have a priority
060   * less than {@link Command#DEFAULT_PRIORITY} so it doesn't prevent low-priority commands from
061   * running.
062   *
063   * <p>The default command is initially an idle command that only owns the mechanism without doing
064   * anything. This command has the lowest possible priority to allow any other command to run.
065   *
066   * @param defaultCommand the new default command
067   */
068  default void setDefaultCommand(Command defaultCommand) {
069    getRegisteredScheduler().setDefaultCommand(this, defaultCommand);
070  }
071
072  /**
073   * Gets the default command that was set by the latest call to {@link
074   * #setDefaultCommand(Command)}.
075   *
076   * @return The currently configured default command
077   */
078  default Command getDefaultCommand() {
079    return getRegisteredScheduler().getDefaultCommandFor(this);
080  }
081
082  /**
083   * Starts building a command that requires this mechanism.
084   *
085   * @param commandBody The main function body of the command.
086   * @return The command builder, for further configuration.
087   */
088  default NeedsNameBuilderStage run(Consumer<Coroutine> commandBody) {
089    return new StagedCommandBuilder().requiring(this).executing(commandBody);
090  }
091
092  /**
093   * Starts building a command that requires this mechanism. The given function will be called
094   * repeatedly in an infinite loop. Useful for building commands that don't need state or multiple
095   * stages of logic.
096   *
097   * @param loopBody The body of the infinite loop.
098   * @return The command builder, for further configuration.
099   */
100  default NeedsNameBuilderStage runRepeatedly(Runnable loopBody) {
101    return run(
102        coroutine -> {
103          while (true) {
104            loopBody.run();
105            coroutine.yield();
106          }
107        });
108  }
109
110  /**
111   * Returns a command that idles this mechanism until another command claims it. The idle command
112   * has {@link Command#LOWEST_PRIORITY the lowest priority} and can be interrupted by any other
113   * command.
114   *
115   * <p>The {@link #getDefaultCommand() default command} for every mechanism is an idle command
116   * unless a different default command has been configured.
117   *
118   * @return A new idle command.
119   */
120  default Command idle() {
121    return run(Coroutine::park).withPriority(Command.LOWEST_PRIORITY).named(getName() + "[IDLE]");
122  }
123
124  /**
125   * Returns a command that idles this mechanism for the given duration of time.
126   *
127   * @param duration How long the mechanism should idle for.
128   * @return A new idle command.
129   */
130  default Command idleFor(Time duration) {
131    return idle().withTimeout(duration);
132  }
133
134  /**
135   * Gets all running commands that require this mechanism. Commands are returned in the order in
136   * which they were scheduled. The returned list is read-only. Every command in the list will have
137   * been scheduled by the previous entry in the list or by intermediate commands that do not
138   * require the mechanism.
139   *
140   * @return The currently running commands that require the mechanism.
141   */
142  @NoDiscard
143  default List<Command> getRunningCommands() {
144    return getRegisteredScheduler().getRunningCommandsFor(this);
145  }
146}
